set.hook: Pupillin's village auberge, starred in March 2026, cooking snails, trout and Bresse hen with Jura wine.
set.why: Vivien Sonzogni and Noémie Paris took over the Grapiot in 2024 with partners who mostly met at catering school in Poligny, helped by a Gault&Millau young-talent grant. Two years later came the first MICHELIN star, the Jura's third. The kitchen works with Morteau, cancoillotte, Planches trout and Bresse poultry; the cellar is almost all Jura, and the wine bar on the lower terrace won a Cep d'Or 2025 for its Poulsard service. Pierre Overnoy's domaine is a few doors away.
set.verdict: The most exciting table on the slope this year, and still priced like a village restaurant: 60 euros buys the starred kitchen. Gault&Millau 2026 gives 14.5/20 and calls the Bresse hen with morels exemplary. Hours differ between listings, so call before driving, and pair lunch here with a Pupillin cellar visit rather than making it a late dinner run from Lons.

set.caveat: Closed Monday; Sunday dinner and weekday hours disputed between listings; book by phone; about 30 km from Lons

set.hook: Arbois Bib Gourmand by the Cuisance, run by two Jeunet-trained cooks, with an all-Jura wine list.
set.why: Jérôme Brousseau cooks and Lisa Vuillemin makes the desserts; both came up through the Jeunet kitchen in Arbois and took this room on the Faramand in 2019. The house plate is a ballottine of Planches trout stuffed with morels and oyster mushrooms in a Vin Jaune sauce, river fish from a few kilometres upstream. MICHELIN made it its Bib of the month in October 2023, and the wine list stays inside the Jura.
set.verdict: The sensible lunch on the slope: the 'Au fil du jour' menu is what MICHELIN calls unbeatable value, and Gault&Millau 2026 rates the kitchen 13/20 and the town's leading table. It is bistro cooking with serious technique, not a tasting-menu event. From November the Thursday dinner goes, so plan Arbois evenings for Tuesday, Wednesday, Friday or Saturday.

set.caveat: Closed Sunday and Monday, and Thursday evenings November-March; book lunch; about 40 km from Lons

set.name: La Chaumière
set.hook: Dole's starred inn: Laurent Barberot's tasting menu Friday and Saturday, his bistrot La Bagatelle on weekdays.
set.why: A hotel-restaurant with a garden and a pool on the avenue du Maréchal Juin, on the edge of Dole. Joël Césari held the star here for years; when he retired, Laurent Barberot, a Vesoul native who trained with Bernard Loiseau, Laurent Petit and Jacques Chibois and cooked at the Plaza Athénée and La Pyramide, took over (reported May 2025). At the weekend he serves one seasonal menu with Jura touches such as smoked eel, Bresse poultry and Jura cheeses; on weekdays the same room becomes the bistrot.
set.verdict: The third star on the Jura list and the only one where the gastronomic menu runs on two days a week, so plan the grand night for Friday or Saturday. Gault&Millau 2026 gives 13.5/20 and says Barberot is changing the house gradually. The weekday bistrot is the easier, cheaper way in. It is a long drive from Lons for dinner: pair it with Pasteur's Dole by day.

set.caveat: About 50 km north of Lons (A39); the starred menu only Friday evening to Saturday evening, bistrot the rest of the week; phone not verified

set.hook: A 32-cover bistro on rue Émile Monot with a short regional menu built for sharing.
set.why: The dining room sits a few steps below the street, small enough that the kitchen is never far. The menu is short, three or four starters and mains, and diners say it changes monthly. set.hook: A roadside auberge on the Besançon road keeping the Jura classics, ending on a Macvin soufflé glacé.
set.why: Out on the route de Besançon at the northern edge of Lons, with free parking at the door, this is where the region's classic plates are cooked straight: a crust of morels in Vin Jaune, Jura trout with roasted bacon, and for dessert a soufflé glacé flavoured with Macvin, the Jura's grape-must-and-marc aperitif, or griottine cherries from Fougerolles. Gault&Millau calls it quiet and steady.
set.verdict: A safe traditional dinner close to town, rated 11/20 by Gault&Millau, with the 47 euro Menu des Gourmets as the full tour. Diner reviews are mixed: an August 2026 TripAdvisor review complained of a cool welcome and prices, while others praise the cooking. Go for the classics and the soufflé, not for a polished service.
set.caveat: Hours disputed between listings (Saturday especially); a car or taxi from the centre; reviews mention cool service

set.hook: Half Lyon bouchon, half Jura kitchen, with meat grilled on a wood stove in the middle of the room.
set.why: The menu runs on two tracks: Lyonnais bouchon plates such as tablier de sapeur, breaded and fried tripe, beside Jura recipes such as an oeuf cocotte with Comté and Macvin sauce. The meat is grilled on a wood-burning stove set in the centre of the dining room, so the room smells of the fire. Gault&Millau 2026 calls it Lons's institutional brasserie, where people come for business lunches.
set.verdict: A reliable, generous table rather than a fine one: Gault&Millau's 2026 entry keeps it in the guide with a market menu at 37.95 euros, and recent reviews praise the welcome. Order from the fire or the pike quenelle. Hours vary between listings, but it serves both lunch and dinner on most weekdays, which makes it the easiest booking in town.

set.name: La Finette, Taverne d'Arbois
set.hook: Arbois's log-table tavern since 1961: Comté fondue, poulet au Vin Jaune, an all-Jura wine list.
set.why: La Finette has fed Arbois since 1961 from a timber-built room off avenue Pasteur: varnished log tables set round barrels, folk décor on every wall and a vaulted cellar below. The food is the Jura farmhouse canon served in quantity, from a pot of Comté fondue kept bubbling at the table to chicken deglazed with Vin Jaune and morels, Morteau sausage and Jura trout. The wine list stays inside the department, so it doubles as a first lesson in Savagnin and Trousseau.
set.verdict: Go for the room and the classics, not for finesse. Gault&Millau 2026 gives it 11/20 and says the technique does not always convince, probably because of the crowds, while praising the terrace, the mood and generous plates. Diners rate it highly on Google (4.6 from about 2,700 reviews). Order the fondue or the Vin Jaune chicken and drink a local bottle.

set.caveat: In Arbois, about 40 km north of Lons by road; busy at weekends and in season, so book; hours vary by source, call ahead

set.hook: Arbois's natural-wine cave à manger: one lunch dish a day, a cold buffet, a shelf of local bottles.
set.why: On Place Faramand in Arbois, the Claquets is a bar first: open from breakfast to about 9 in the evening, with a shelf of local natural wines instead of a printed list. At noon the kitchen sends out a single dish of the day with a buffet of cold starters, a formula Le Fooding priced at 12 € a plate and 16 to 19.50 € for the set. Growers come in for lunch, and some evenings there is music.
set.verdict: The cheapest serious lunch on the Arbois side and the easiest place to drink Arbois natural wine without an appointment. There is no choice at lunch, which is the point. June 2026 visitors on Raisin praise the room and the value. Book by phone for lunch; the tables go fast.
set.signature: The plat du jour with the cold-starter buffet, and a glass from the shelf
set.caveat: Lunch booking by phone only; closed Sunday and Monday; posted autumn break 23 Oct-1 Nov (year not stated); about 40 km from Lons

set.hook: The Jura's biggest weekly market: Thursday food on Place de Verdun, a Saturday organic market on Cours Sully.
set.why: On Thursday Lons fills two squares: a morning food market on Place de Verdun and a day of clothes and hardware on Place du 11 Novembre, from about 7 until 5. Saturday morning is smaller and food only, organic and short-chain stalls on Cours Sully. Late October is when Mont d'Or comes back in its spruce box, beside Comté of several ages, Morteau sausages with their wooden plug, jars of cancoillotte and fir honey.
set.verdict: Thursday morning is the one to plan around: the food stalls are on Place de Verdun and thin out by midday. Saturday is the quieter, greener version. The new mayor, elected in March 2026, has tested moving the Thursday market to Place de la Liberté and rue du Commerce, so check the squares before you go.
set.signature: Comté at two or three ages from one stall, and a Mont d'Or for the boat oven
set.caveat: Thursday food is mornings only; a permanent move to Place de la Liberté is under study, check the location

set.name: Chez l'Artisan Fromager
set.hook: A cheesemaking family's own counter under the rue du Commerce arcades: Morbier first, then raclette and tomme.
set.why: The Poulet family have made cheese for four generations, and this shop at no. 39 rue du Commerce sells what they make: raclette cheese, tomme du Jura and above all Morbier. It sits under the stone arcades in the middle of Lons, so you can step out of the November rain into the smell of rind and cellar. Jura Tourisme lists it as both shop and producer, and the counter speaks French, German, Spanish and Italian.
set.verdict: The best-evidenced cheese counter in central Lons and the right replacement for a Comté affineur the old guide placed here by mistake. Come for the Morbier, which is the family's own; for a run of Comté ages, the Thursday market stalls may serve you better. Hours conflict and nothing dated 2026 turned up, so check before carrying a cool bag across town.
set.caveat: Hours conflict between directories and no 2026-dated evidence was found: call or pass by first

set.name: Chocolaterie Pelen
set.hook: Lons's family chocolatier since 1899, roasting its own beans, with a tea room upstairs.
set.why: Joseph Pelen opened as confectioner and chocolatier in 1899, and the house kept the Prince d'Orange name he took in 1902. The boutique on rue Saint-Désiré is Belle Époque and runs over two floors, with a tea room upstairs. Pelen is one of very few French chocolatiers to roast its own cocoa beans, and Arnaud Pelen, of the family, makes the praliné. Regulars come back for the écureuil, the squirrel-shaped house speciality.
set.verdict: The chocolate shop Lons is known for, and the place for an edible gift to carry back aboard. Gault&Millau lists it as an artisan. Recent reviews are mixed: praise for the pastries and the écureuil, complaints about prices, early closing and a cool welcome, with a newer note that the tea room has improved. Buy the chocolate; do not count on a late coffee.
set.signature: The écureuil, and the Galet de Chalain praliné-nougatine
set.caveat: The shop is 1 rue Saint-Désiré in the centre; rue Blaise Pascal is the industrial-zone site. Tea room closes early
